Upstream Eller cycle — recorded so the reason for the union-find is never lost.

Source: docs/sources/maze-inventory.md §4.3 and §9 M-1; decision
docs/decisions/maze.md §5 M-1. Not reproducible by this test binary on purpose:
fbs_maze never had the defect, so there is nothing here to run.

The instance, measured by the maze-research worker against a faithful C
re-implementation of Eller.cpp plus FRandomStream:

  algorithm : Eller (LowkeyMe UE5-MazeGenerator-Plugin, Eller.cpp)
  seed      : 42
  grid      : 6 x 6 direction cells (the plugin's MazeSize 11 x 11)
  cells     : 36
  edges     : 36        <- a perfect maze of 36 cells has exactly 35
  components: 1
  verdict   : one surplus edge, i.e. exactly one cycle

Cause, in one line: Eller.cpp:38-43 and :95-100 relabel only the contiguous
run starting at X+1 when two sets merge, where Buck's reference relabels every
cell of the dissolved set. A set that sent two south passages down with a gap
between them occupies non-contiguous columns in the next row, so the last-row
join loop later reconnects two regions that were already connected through the
rows above. Census over sizes 5-41 x 500 seeds: 4,474 of 9,500 mazes contain at
least one cycle, 8,169 surplus edges in total, worst case 9 in one maze; the
failure rate is 1% at MazeSize 7, 46% at 21 and 94% at 41, while README.md:94
claims "Generated mazes are perfect".

What fbs_maze does instead (src/maze.c, maze_eller): a real union-find over the
row, so a merge joins whole sets and a passage is never carved between two cells
that already share one. MT-2 asserts the result — passage_count == w*h - 1 and an
independent DFS finding no back edge — for all eight algorithms over the whole
size x seed matrix, and MT-10a asserts the second Eller defect (M-2) is gone too.
